Description: Normal
Resolution steps: Normal

Summary: One or more hashboards were not detected
Description: The hashboard PLUG signal was not detected
Error information: Detected hashboard numbers, separated by spaces if there is more than one
Resolution steps:
1. Check the SPI ribbon connection against a working machine. Disconnect and reconnect the ribbon.
2. Replace the control board.
3. Replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Description: Abnormal power-supply I2C communication
Resolution steps:
1. Replace the power supply.
2. Replace the control board.

Description: SPI communication fails on all hashboards
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
2. Replace the power supply.
3. Replace the control board.
4. Return the complete machine for repair.

Description: SPI communication fails on some hashboards
Error information: Hashboard numbers with failed SPI communication, separated by spaces if there is more than one
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
2. Replace the power supply.
3. Replace the control board.
4. Replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Description: Hashboard frequency increase failed
Error information: Hashboard number: frequency at which the error occurred
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
2. Replace the power supply.
3. Replace the control board.
4. Replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Description: Voltage setting failed
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
2. Replace the power supply.
3. Replace the control board.
4. Replace the faulty hashboard (board assembly).

Description: Chip BIST test failed
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.

Summary: Abnormal hashboard communication during operation cannot recover automatically
Description: Abnormal hashboard SPI communication during operation cannot recover automatically
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
2. Replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Summary: Abnormal power-supply communication during operation cannot recover automatically
Description: Abnormal power-supply I2C communication during operation cannot recover automatically
Resolution steps:
1. Replace the power supply.
2. Replace the control board.

Summary: Connection to the mining pool is interrupted
Description: Connection to the mining pool is interrupted
Resolution steps:
If many or all miners on the same switch have this problem:
1. Check the mining-pool settings.
2. Check the network configuration, such as DHCP, DNS, and ports.
If only one or a few miners have this problem:
1. Check the mining-pool settings.
2. Check that the miner network-port connection is secure.
3. Exchange the network cable with that of a working miner.
4. Replace the control board.

Summary: Damage to individual chips causes a falsely high displayed machine hash rate
Description: Damage to individual chips causes a falsely high displayed machine hash rate
Error information: Damaged chip number: hashboard number; separate multiple entries with spaces
Resolution steps: No action is required.

Description: Hashboard overtemperature
Resolution steps:
1. Check whether the front and rear fans turn. If they do not, replace the fans first. If this does not help, replace the control board or power supply.
2. Check that the front and rear airflow directions agree and match the other machines. If they do not, change the fan orientation.
3. Measure the miner inlet temperature. If it is above 40 degrees, improve the mining-facility temperature conditions.
4. If one hashboard frequently overheats, replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Description: Cannot read the chip temperature
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
2. Replace the power supply.
3. Replace the control board.
4. Replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Summary: The control-board communication ribbon is connected incorrectly
Description: Abnormal control-board SPI ribbon connection
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the hashboard SPI ribbon connection method and sequence match other machines of the same model.
2. Replace the control board.

Description: Abnormal power delivery
Resolution steps:
1. If the machine hash rate has no obvious abnormality and no board goes offline, no action is required.
2. Check that the screws at both ends of the power terminals and the SPI ribbon connections are not loose.
3. Replace the power supply.

Summary: Some chips do not operate correctly
Description: Abnormal number of good chip cores
Resolution steps:
1. If the machine hash rate has no obvious abnormality and no board goes offline, no action is required.
2. Restart the miner and check whether the same error remains.
3. Replace the faulty hashboard (return the board assembly for repair).

Summary: Control-board type, firmware version, and chip count do not match
Description: Control-board type, firmware version, and chip count do not match
Resolution steps: When more than 10 affected machines have accumulated, contact software R&D to resolve them together.

Summary: Low hash rate on the last few chips
Description: Low hash rate on the last few chip stages
Resolution steps: No action is currently required.

Description: The initial burn-in frequency and voltage are incorrect
Resolution steps: No action is currently required.

Notes:
1. After each resolution step, turn the power off and on to check whether normal operation has returned.
2. If replacement of a part does not resolve the problem, put the removed part back in its original machine.
3. Attach the error code and a short problem description to every hashboard confirmed for return for repair.
